semantics: Normative state machine is /stop_protocol. All readers, writers and reapers must use it; signatures alone are insufficient.

StopIntent identifiers are data, not authority. Only coordinator-issued, nontransferable StopExecutor object identity has execution authority. The coordinator checks the current incarnation, operation and owner fencing on every call and every lease.signal.

admit durably prepares before returning. Exactly one caller obtains executor; all concurrent requests for the same job incarnation join the SAME unresolved intent regardless of caller/call ID. Joiners cannot acquire a signal lease or signal.
join waits without a metadata transaction, then calls terminal_guard. Timeout returns unresolved unknown with outcome_persisted=False or raises a controlled error; it never starts a second executor.

quiesce is idempotent, blocks until in-flight signal calls finish, invalidates every lease signal entrypoint and closes owned signal handles. Failure to prove quiescence prevents resolution. It does not reap a child.

record checks coordinator-held evidence, not caller-supplied receipt booleans, and resolves only the same prepared operation after full closure, terminal leader proof and executor quiescence. No success before file AND directory sync. Failed/unknown receipts leave prepare unresolved.

terminal_guard returns None only for a positively readable record with no stop intent or legacy uncertainty. For any unresolved/failed/unreadable/ambiguous state it raises JobSignalDeliveryError (Linux) or AuthorityUnknown (Darwin). Closed receipts are returned only after all resolution barriers. None is not authorization to infer leader exit; ordinary verified exit policy still applies.

A1 exclusively implements Linux coordinator/storage/read/reaper/RPC/retention and stop_with_intent orchestration. B0a declares this shared seam only; later B0 preserves controlled errors from A1 APIs and never edits A1 paths. R1/CR1 independently reviews complete A1 safety.

semantics: Call admit. If executor is None, join the returned intent with a bounded timeout; never open signals on the joining path. Executor path opens one lease, TERM, observe complete closure, optionally KILL on the same lease, observe again.

In finally, close the lease and quiesce the executor before record. Record only evidence for this exact intent; a failed/unknown result preserves unresolved prepare. Closed success requires target_set_closed, leader_terminal, executor_quiesced and outcome_persisted all true after checked barriers.

No metadata lock held across signals/waits. A1 coordinator owns the execution fence and terminal guards. Existing stop_embedded stays import compatible; A1 routes all actual Linux repaired stops through this seam and prevents legacy bypasses. B0 never edits the Linux engine.

semantics: RootGrant and OpenedFile own descriptors; idempotent close, use-after-close rejected. Caller closes in finally; app lifetime owns grants.

Captured configured canonical root is opened once. Traverse relative components with dir_fd and no-follow checks; reject absolute path, dotdot, symlink/reparse ambiguity. Never reopen an authorized pathname.

Opened-object semantics: grant follows the original directory object across rename, never replacement path. Newly encountered moved/symlink objects are rejected if authority cannot be proved. No continuous pathname confinement or hostile same-UID guarantee.
Regular files only for content. Read has a hard byte budget. Missing/denied/TCC-possible paths never become empty results.

write_bytes owns parent FD, temporary file, flush/fsync/rename cleanup. expected_sha256 guards detected content conflicts for edits, not hostile concurrent-writer serializability. No follow of existing symlink; reject hardlinked mutation unless writing a replacement entry.

Search enumerates through grant and supplies each authorized open regular file to rg stdin, uses bounded resources and remaps stdin events to relative display path. Never pass an unchecked root path or /dev/fd directory to recursive rg. Ignore/glob parity requires native tests; unsupported cases error explicitly.

metadata uses fstat on the same opened regular file; read enforces max_bytes against actual bytes even if file grows. Display paths are formatting only. Core cannot call exists/stat/read_bytes on display paths.

list_entries owns all directory descriptors and traversal. ListRequest.glob=None means bounded one-level dirs-first listing; glob means bounded recursive authorized traversal with existing ignore/hidden policy and newest-first ordering. FileListing.truncated reports budget exhaustion, never silently claims exhaustive results. No recursive pathname rg --files.

write_bytes(create_parents=True) creates each missing parent with mkdir relative to a verified descriptor then opens and verifies it no-follow before continuing; never Path.mkdir. Enforce max_new_parents and fail explicitly on exhausted budget. Default False for edits. Parent creation may remain after later write failure; no all-operation rollback claim.

WriteReceipt derives previous_bytes/action from the descriptor-verified destination at the write step, not a prior Core pathname stat. For expected_sha256 require an existing regular file and compare its opened bytes before replacement; mismatch or disappearance fails. This detects observed conflicts, not atomic compare-and-swap against hostile writers.

nearby_hint enumerates only the deepest authorized existing parent using the same grant and no-follow traversal with a hard result bound; inaccessible/ambiguous parents yield no hint with the original explicit error preserved. Never open an unauthorized ancestor to improve a diagnostic.

SearchRequest maps the current tool smart-case/ignore/hidden defaults; unsupported policy combinations fail explicitly. Ignore files and ancestor rules can be read only through authorized descriptors; if semantics would require outside-root reads, refuse that mode. No environmental config may widen scope.

B0 dispatches every operation in /file_tool_wiring to A4 adapters, including both list modes, parent creation and diagnostics; default Linux path remains unchanged. Missing Darwin adapter is CapabilityUnavailable, never Linux/path fallback.

admission: Serialize metadata read/merge/prepare and ownership decisions across processes using one stable owned lock domain per job incarnation; a process-local RLock, lock timeout or replaceable lock inode is insufficient. All store writers and retention use the same transaction boundary.

One active executor reservation per job incarnation, including outstanding operations from older owner epochs. Concurrent callers join its request_id; no alternate request/lease may bypass unresolved admission.

Persist an immutable unresolved prepare record with job incarnation, owner epoch and operation ID before opening signals: bounded temp write, flush, file fsync, atomic replace, directory fsync including newly created ancestor entries. Every error, including post-replace directory fsync, refuses admission and permits zero signals.

Keep the prepare record independently of the tentative resolution. Establish the executor lifetime fence before admission and keep it until quiescence. Do not hold metadata transactions across native signals, join waits or reaper waits.
execution: Only the executor token opens one validated signal lease; TERM and optional KILL use that same lease. No numeric reacquisition or second child waiter. Close membership/birth admission and verify complete authorized target coverage; a disappearing leader, empty snapshot or reaper exit record is insufficient.

The sole existing owning waiter publishes leader exit evidence through a merge transaction that preserves prepare/partial flags and operation identity. Reaper publication never resolves a stop. Metrics/history finalization uses the same merge guard.

Partial delivery, failed diagnostic persistence, cancellation or loss leaves the prior durable prepare intact. Prevent future signal entry, wait for in-flight calls, close leases and establish executor quiescence in finally; lack of proof stays unresolved.
resolution: Reject resolution without the exact prepared identity or with a stale/mismatched executor. Require independently checked full target-set closure, terminal leader evidence and quiescence of the sole executor before making a tentative closed receipt.

Write and fsync tentative resolution, atomically replace, then fsync its directory under the common transaction. Only after all barriers succeed may the coordinator set outcome_persisted=True and release a closed result. Prepare remains available for crash reconciliation.

Visible closed bytes after failed directory sync are UNCOMMITTED. Invalidate cached success, retain unresolved prepare and raise. Readers cannot trust disk state=closed, exit_code, signal or ended_at in isolation.

On restart or absence of a live commit acknowledgment, a guarded recovery transaction must validate the matching prepare/resolution and closure evidence, positively fence/quiesce the old executor, and successfully re-sync the resolution file and directory before terminal acceptance. If any evidence is unavailable, retain UNKNOWN. A visible receipt or new owner epoch alone cannot authorize recovery.
terminal_reads: Run terminal_guard within the same read/merge transaction on EVERY terminal path: stop retry, job_state/list_jobs, await_exit including timeout, owner RPC before ok=true, local fallback, command status and restart recovery. Resolve before ordinary exited mapping; expose the existing controlled error envelope if unresolved, without adding Linux wire states or fields.

Guard result and terminal metadata must come from one transaction/version; copying an earlier guard result across a concurrent admission is forbidden. Reaper-only terminal reads may retain internal leader evidence but cannot publish completed stop.

Legacy stop_requested or stop_signal_partial without a verified resolution, missing/corrupt/unreadable metadata or journal, uncertain durability and unknown ownership block success. Missing metadata in an existing job directory is uncertainty, not a nonexistent job.
retention_restart: Retention cannot remove any unresolved intent, legacy uncertain stop, unreadable job or required prepare/resolution/closure evidence, including resource-history rows needed for resolution. Recheck eligibility under the shared transaction immediately before deletion.

Recovery cannot relabel uncertainty as stopped, adopt persisted PIDs or launch a successor signal executor until the previous executor is positively proven quiescent. Require live cooperative drain acknowledgment or non-inherited exclusive lifetime ownership with proven release; lease timeout, PID absence, generation change or broken socket is insufficient.
Restart and rollback quiet gates treat unresolved/unknown jobs as active. No stable manager restart while such jobs remain.
compatibility: Linux v1/v2 legacy metadata, combined output and byte cursors remain readable; RPC protocol stays 1. Prepare/resolution data are internal additive state, never new public tool fields. New owner with old client returns existing error envelope for uncertainty.

Old-owner/new-client compatibility must be tested, but the unchanged old owner cannot be credited with the new stop guarantees. Full repaired-stop acceptance requires all writers/readers owning that spool to implement the barriers; mixed unsafe old owners remain an explicit limitation.

foreground_execution.mechanism: The live spawning process uses posix_spawn (Python os.posix_spawn with setpgroup=0 or a public native equivalent) to start bash -c in a new process group whose leader is its unreaped direct child. No shell launched via Linux durable engine.
signal_reap_order: Only that same live spawning process can signal the originally created group. Serialize leader-reaped state and all group signal calls under a single owner-local lock. No other thread, SIGCHLD handler, Popen poll/wait path or background waiter may reap this child.

Do not infer alive from PID lookup. Kernel parenthood plus sole ownership of an unreaped child anchors the identity; no adoption from PID/PGID metadata. Reserve the unreaped leader until all permitted cleanup signals finish. After any successful reap, invalidate group authority before releasing the lock; never signal again.

Timeout/cancel/over-limit uses bounded TERM then KILL if needed, while leader remains unreaped, then reaps exactly once. If leader has already been reaped, refuse further group signals and report descendants_unverified. Signal errors or failure to reap/close resources return explicit failure; never claim whole-tree cleanup.

Normal completion requires sole-owner wait evidence and bounded output drain; escaped descendants may keep pipe FDs open, so pipe EOF cannot cause an unbounded wait. Close pipes on drain budget exhaustion and report truncation.
background_policy: background=true or requested wait_seconds exceeding foreground_limit_s is refused before spawn with darwin_background_jobs_unavailable. If a group already exists when background/over-limit is detected, kill it under the unreaped-leader rule before returning that error. Do not spawn merely to reject a request.

A running command reaching min(wait_seconds, foreground_limit_s) gets owned-group cleanup and darwin_background_jobs_unavailable; never return running/background_job=true or auto-background it. foreground_limit_s is positive, at most captured settings.wait_max_s (base maximum 50 seconds); no mutable per-call widening.

Cancellation initiates the same bounded group cleanup before request teardown and propagates a controlled cancellation/error. If owner authority is lost, report UNKNOWN/error; never delegate numeric group killing to a replacement process.
scope_limits: setsid/double-fork or otherwise escaped descendants are outside authority; every result declares descendants_unverified=true and descriptions state this limit. Foreground means bounded owner wait, not complete descendant containment.

Owner death may leave the command unsupervised. Later history/status is UNKNOWN; no adoption or signaling by a restarted owner. A previously durably recorded leader exit can remain leader-only history, never descendant closure.
stop_job remains UNAVAILABLE. job_status is history/output only. No durable background execution or stable-manager continuation is promised.
